description: Unified dashboard for monitoring AgentGateway (OSS & Enterprise) - AI Gateway with rate limiting, content guardrails, and MCP support. Enhanced with organized metrics sections: Core GenAI metrics (all requests), Streaming metrics (requires stream=true), and Model-specific breakdowns. | Pricing source-of-truth: see Cost Tracking section, last updated 2026-06-05.

panels.title: Total Requests
panels.description: Total requests through the gateway over the selected time range. The sparkline shows how that traffic was distributed across the range. The total is a sum of per-interval increases, so it can drift slightly from a single whole-range increase.
Current request throughput across all gateway traffic (LLM and MCP), as requests per second over the most recent rate interval.
panels.title: Request Rate
Total Input Tokens
panels.description: Total LLM input (prompt) tokens over the selected time range, with trend.

panels.title: Total Output Tokens
panels.description: Total LLM output (completion) tokens over the selected time range, with trend.

panels.title: MCP Requests
panels.description: Total MCP protocol requests (tool calls, list operations, initialize, and so on) over the selected time range. Reads "0 requests" when no MCP traffic is flowing through the gateway.

panels.title: Avg Tokens per LLM Request
panels.description: Average input and output tokens per LLM request over the selected time range. The denominator is the LLM request count (gen_ai_server_request_duration_count), not total gateway requests, so this stays correct when non-LLM traffic (for example MCP) also flows through the gateway.

panels.title: Error Rate (4xx)
panels.description: Share of requests returning a 4xx status other than 429 over the selected time range, with the absolute error count. Yellow above 1%, red above 5%.

panels.title: Error Rate (429)
panels.description: Share of requests returning 429 (rate limited) over the selected time range, with the absolute count. Thresholds are laxer than the other error tiles (yellow above 5%, red above 20%) because rate limiting is often intentional policy, not failure.

panels.title: Error Rate (5xx)
panels.description: Share of requests returning a 5xx status over the selected time range, with the absolute error count. Yellow above 1%, red above 5%.

Request throughput split by status class. Success (2xx) is deliberately muted gray so error classes stand out: 4xx yellow (client errors, excluding 429), 429 orange (rate limited), 5xx red (server errors). A spike here that never shows in the range-total tiles is exactly what those tiles cannot tell you.
panels.title: Requests by Status Class

panels.description: p95 latency over time on a log scale, because the series live on different orders of magnitude. LLM end-to-end is gen_ai_server_request_duration (includes token generation). LLM TTFT is upstream_call_duration_seconds, which for LLM traffic measures time to first token. MCP is request_duration_seconds for routes matching 'mcp', typically tens of milliseconds. This panel replaces the old P95 Latency (LLM) and P95 Latency (MCP) stat tiles.
panels.title: LLM Latency Percentiles (p95)

panels.description: p95 of the request-path leg only, from receiving the request to sending the first outbound call. Policy callouts land in this leg, and it accounts for about 98% of gateway overhead; the response leg averages 0.3ms. Percentiles are not additive, so the response leg is not summed in. Colored yellow above 10ms and red above 100ms of gateway-added latency.
panels.title: P95 Request-Path Overhead

panels.description: p99 of the request-path leg, from receiving the request to sending the first outbound call, which is where policy callouts land. Compare against P95 Request-Path Overhead: a p99 well above p95 means a subset of requests pays a cost the rest avoid, such as an intermittently slow policy callout, a cold JWKS or token cache, or an outsized request body. Upstream LLM and MCP wait time is excluded. Colored yellow above 10ms and red above 100ms of gateway-added latency.
panels.title: P99 Request-Path Overhead

panels.description: Gateway overhead as a share of total request latency (computed from means, because a ratio of percentiles has no meaning), shown next to the absolute mean overhead. The percentage alone can look alarming when upstreams are fast (for example mock model servers), so only the absolute value carries color: yellow above 10ms, red above 100ms. A high percentage with a sub-millisecond absolute value means the gateway is fine and the upstream is just quick.
panels.title: Gateway Overhead % of Latency
Token Usage by Model
panels.description: Per-model traffic and token usage over the selected time range. Share of Requests is each model's fraction of known-model LLM requests (requests with an unknown gen_ai_response_model are excluded), so heavy hitters are obvious without mental division.
Combined input+output token throughput per model. Pairs with the table: the table gives range totals, this shows when each model was busy.
panels.title: Token Rate by Model

panels.title: Total Cost
panels.description: Total LLM spend over the last hour and last 24 hours, plus a projected 30-day figure, from hardcoded per-model prices in the queries (see the pricing tables at the bottom of this section). Unknown models are excluded - watch Untracked Cost. Use the dashboard time picker for other windows. "projected 30d" scales the observed spend run-rate to 30 days using the actual data coverage in the 7-day window, so it is honest on fresh clusters and equals a plain 7d x 30/7 projection once a full week of history exists.
Mean cost per LLM request across all priced models, over the dashboard time range.

panels.description: Stacked per-model breakdown of cache_read and cache_write spend. Anthropic, Bedrock-Anthropic and OpenAI gpt-5.6 models show both series; older OpenAI models show cache_read only (no write fee). Replaces the old token-throughput view — same shape, but priced so you can see where cache dollars actually concentrate.
panels.title: Cache Spend by Model ($/hour)

panels.description: Per-model breakdown of token throughput for models not in the canonical pricing list. Add them to the pricing list to start tracking cost.
panels.title: Untracked Token Throughput by Model

panels.description: Per-request distribution of cached prefix size (input_cache_read tokens). This is the prompt prefix being reused on each turn — large system prompts, loaded skills, MCP tool definitions, etc. p95 jumps when context bloats; investigate by checking which skills/tools were added since the jump.
panels.title: Cache Read Tokens Per Request (Context Size)

panels.description: Per-request distribution of cache write size (input_cache_write tokens). First request of a session pays a large cache_write to populate the prefix; steady-state turns should be small or zero. Persistent large p95 means the cache is being invalidated and rewritten — usually because the 'stable' prefix isn't actually stable (skill order changing, tool defs drifting, etc.).
panels.title: Cache Write Tokens Per Request (Cache Churn)

panels.description: p95 cached prefix size broken out by response model. Identifies which model/workload is responsible for context bloat (e.g. opus carrying 127k cached tokens per turn while mini carries 4k). Use this to target which skill/MCP loadouts to trim.

panels.description: Gateway-side latency by leg and route. The request path, from receiving the request to sending the first outbound call, carries the policy callouts; the response path averages 0.3ms. A rising request-path p95 on one route points at a policy on that route, and upstream slowness appears in Upstream Call Duration by Callout Class instead.
panels.title: Gateway Processing Latency by Route (p95)

panels.description: Duration of every outbound call the gateway makes, by class: Primary/Llm and Primary/Mcp are the upstreams, Policy/* are policy callouts such as the rate limiter, ext-auth, and WAF. For streaming LLM traffic this measures time to first token rather than full request duration, because the call is timed until the upstream begins responding. Primary/Llm tracks gen_ai_server_time_to_first_token to within 0.14% on live traffic and reads about half of gen_ai_server_request_duration; use P95 Latency (LLM) or GenAI Request Duration for end-to-end model latency. Only kind and subtype labels are present, so this cannot be sliced by route or model.
panels.title: Upstream Call Duration by Callout Class
